Enum Class Equivalence

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<Equivalence>
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.map.Equivalence
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<Equivalence>, Constable
public enum Equivalence extends Enum<Equivalence>
Degree of correspondence between the key and the value of a mapping Entry.

The vocabulary and its direction are those of FHIR R4 ConceptMap (element.target.equivalence): the relation is read from the value (the target) to the key (the source). WIDER means that the value is the wider concept, as other is wider than A (adoption). R4's subsumes and specializes fold onto WIDER and NARROWER.

Its purpose here is to state which entries may be used to build the reverse index of a Mapping: only entries that assert an EQUAL or EQUIVALENT correspondence are invertible. A key whose value is WIDER does not become the canonical inverse of that value, which is what makes reverse-direction collisions detectable instead of silent.

Since:
6.0

    • isTranslation

      public boolean isTranslation()
      Whether an entry with this equivalence is a translation at all, i.e. whether looking up its key should answer with its value. Everything but DISJOINT is: a value that is wider, narrower or only inexactly related to its key is still a translation of it, if an imprecise one. DISJOINT asserts the opposite - that the two are explicitly not equivalent - so answering with its value would state the reverse of what the mapping says.

      FHIR draws the same line: the result of a $translate "can only be true if at least one returned match has an equivalence which is not unmatched or disjoint".

      Returns:
      whether a lookup of this entry's key answers with its value
